title: Holomorphic division by coordinate functions with parameters
statement: Use the usual complex field $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $r,d\geq0$ be integers, and let $H$ be a germ at $(0,0)$ of a holomorphic function on $\mathbf C^r\times\mathbf C^d$. Here a germ is an equivalence class of functions defined on neighbourhoods of $(0,0)$, two representatives being equivalent when they agree on a smaller neighbourhood, and holomorphic means locally given by convergent complex power series. Write $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ and $t=(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$. There exist holomorphic germs $H_1,\ldots,H_r$ at $(0,0)$ such that $$H(z,t)-H(0,t)=\sum_{j=1}^r z_jH_j(z,t).$$ The expression $H(0,t)$ on the left is pulled back along the projection $(z,t)\mapsto t$. If $r=0$, the sum is empty and the equality is $0=0$; $d=0$ is allowed.

proof.text: If r=0 there is nothing to prove, so assume r>0. Choose a representative of the germ and a polydisc centered at (0,0) on which it is represented by an absolutely convergent power series H(z,t)=sum_{alpha in N^r, beta in N^d} c_{alpha,beta} z^alpha t^beta. Shrinking the polydisc if necessary gives a common positive radius rho for all coordinates. Absolute convergence on every smaller closed polydisc permits termwise restriction and rearrangement below.

source.place: WANTED locally: §1 no.1, printed p.3, definition of holomorphic germs by convergent power series; the absolute-convergence property is used in the agent-formulated proof.

proof.text: Setting z=0 kills every monomial with alpha != 0, hence the pulled-back germ H(0,t) is represented by sum_beta c_{0,beta} t^beta. Therefore H(z,t)-H(0,t) is represented by the absolutely convergent subseries sum_{alpha != 0,beta} c_{alpha,beta} z^alpha t^beta.

source.place: WANTED locally: §1 no.1, printed p.3; restriction of a convergent power series to the coordinate subspace.

proof.text: For each alpha != 0 let j(alpha) be the least index with alpha_j>0. For 1<=j<=r define H_j(z,t)=sum_{j(alpha)=j,beta} c_{alpha,beta} z^{alpha-e_j}t^beta. These series converge on a smaller polydisc: if all coordinates have modulus at most s<rho, the absolute value of each divided monomial is at most s^{-1}|c_{alpha,beta}|s^{|alpha|+|beta|}, and the latter terms have a convergent sum; taking a still smaller closed polydisc gives uniform absolute convergence. Thus each H_j defines a holomorphic germ at (0,0).

source.place: WANTED locally: §1 no.1, printed p.3; agent-formulated coefficient-division estimate for convergent multivariable power series.

proof.text: Multiplying the j(alpha)=j summand of H_j by z_j recovers c_{alpha,beta}z^alpha t^beta. The index sets partition all alpha != 0, so absolute convergence justifies summing to obtain H(z,t)-H(0,t)=sum_{j=1}^r z_jH_j(z,t) as germs. If d=0 the same argument has no beta indices; if r=0 the initial empty case gives the required 0=0.
